claim.purpose: Repair guarded prune topology resolution without changing terminal evidence

initial.title: [v0.91.8][csdlc-v2][prune] Resolve issue-local terminal worktree topology safely
initial.goal: Make guarded prune accept the supported issue-local worktree sentinel only for the exact safe checkout.
initial.required_outcome: Guarded prune uses repository-rooted canonical identity, accepts truthful issue-local terminal topology, rejects ambiguous or unsafe checkouts, and never rewrites retained terminal receipts.
declared_scope: Canonical terminal worktree resolution in csdlc-v2 readiness
Focused library and command-level prune regressions
Issue-local typed lifecycle and validation evidence
authority_boundary: Issue 5624 owns only readiness.rs, focused prune tests, and issue-local records
Terminal records and retained receipts remain immutable authority
Issue 5340, Runtime code, and unrelated lifecycle behavior remain outside scope
initial.task_boundary: Replace suffix matching with exact repository-rooted canonical topology matching and prove fail-closed behavior.
deliverables: Canonical resolver for issue-local, absolute, and clean relative terminal worktree identities
Exact branch, current-root, and live-worktree tuple guard
Focused sentinel, collision, traversal, missing, wrong-checkout, dirty, and receipt-stability regressions
Typed validation, review, publication, merge, and terminal receipt
acceptance_criteria: AC-1: `.` resolves to the canonical current issue worktree and passes only for an exact branch and live topology match
AC-2: clean relative worktrees resolve from the primary repository root and absolute worktrees require exact canonical identity
AC-3: empty, missing, traversal-bearing, wrong-branch, wrong-checkout, suffix-collision, and dirty candidates return unsafe_checkout
AC-4: validate-prune leaves retained terminal receipt bytes unchanged
AC-5: a #5340-equivalent closed-out terminal record validates without changing #5340 state or receipt
AC-6: focused Rust tests, strict Clippy, exact-revision review, hosted checks, post-merge validation, and typed closeout pass
dependencies: Issue 5340 terminal evidence as read-only defect provenance
Existing typed C-SDLC v2 binding and Git worktree topology semantics
repo_inputs: Rust standard library and existing tempfile test dependency
non_goals: No terminal schema or record migration
No manual prune bypass or clean-worktree weakening
No Runtime, AWS, provider, or unrelated milestone work
initial.plan_summary: Prepare and bind; add failing topology regressions; implement exact canonical resolution; validate and review; publish, merge, post-merge validate, close out, retain the receipt, and prune only through the repaired guard.

steps.action: Prepare, review, initialize, and bind the issue-local typed lifecycle
Add focused failing regressions and implement exact canonical topology resolution
Run FastWork proof, exact-revision review, and fix every actionable finding
Publish, shepherd exact-head checks, merge, post-merge validate, close out, retain receipt, and guarded-prune if safe

risks: A permissive relative-path rule could prune a same-suffix checkout
A sentinel special case could ignore branch or live topology identity
A repair could accidentally rewrite immutable terminal evidence
A test could prove only a helper while missing command-level behavior
invariants: Eligibility requires exact branch, canonical root, and live Git topology identity
Invalid and ambiguous paths fail with unsafe_checkout
Terminal evidence and retained receipt bytes are unchanged
stop_conditions: Any need to mutate #5340 or migrate terminal records
Any need to change Runtime code, use AWS, or add a dependency
Any proposed rule that accepts suffix-only or traversal-bearing identity
review_prompts: Can `.` validate any checkout other than the exact current terminal branch worktree?
Can two repositories with the same relative worktree suffix collide?
Do malformed, missing, wrong, and dirty candidates fail with unsafe_checkout?
Can validation alter the terminal record or retained receipt?
Does command-level proof exercise the same path as issue 5340?
operator_constraints: No raw gh, AWS, Runtime changes, #5340 mutation, or root-main edits
No approval pauses; complete the authorized issue end to end

validation_lanes.proof_role: Prove exact issue-local, relative, absolute, malformed, wrong-checkout, dirty, and receipt-stability behavior

initial.failure_policy: Fail closed on any non-exact topology, malformed path, receipt drift, validation failure, unresolved review finding, or protected-path expansion.
